title: Pathibhara Devi Yatra Guide: Route, Climb, Heli and Cost
meta_description: Pathibhara Devi yatra guide: route from Siliguri, Kakarbhitta and Bhadrapur, the Kafle Pati climb, helicopter shuttles, best months, costs and packing.
summary: Pathibhara Devi stands at 3,794 m above Phungling in Taplejung, two days by road from the Kakarbhitta border or Bhadrapur airport. Most pilgrims drive to Kafle Pati and climb 4–5 hours; seniors take a pony or a helicopter shuttle. Go in October–November or March–May. Our road yatra costs from ₹26,000 per person.

sections.heading: Who Pathibhara Devi is and where she sits
paras: Pathibhara Devi is a goddess worshipped by Hindus across Nepal, Sikkim, Darjeeling and Bhutan, and by the Limbu people of the eastern hills, who know the mountain as Mukkumlung. Devotees come to ask for a wish to be granted and return to give thanks when it is, leaving brass bells, red and gold cloth, coconuts and, by tradition, animal sacrifices at a separate site below the shrine. Local legend tells of shepherds who lost a large flock on the ridge and were told in a dream to build a shrine there.

The temple itself is small and open to the sky, on a rocky summit at 3,794 m in Taplejung district. On clear mornings Kanchenjunga, at 8,586 m, fills the view to the north-east, with Jannu and the peaks of the Sikkim border beside it. The nearest town is Phungling, the district headquarters at about 1,820 m, and almost every pilgrim sleeps there before and after darshan.

sections.heading: Three ways to reach the shrine
paras: There are three practical ways to do the yatra, and the choice depends mostly on age, fitness and time. The road and walk route is the traditional one and still the most common. The helicopter route saves days and the climb but depends entirely on morning weather. The trekking route uses the old forest trail from Suketar and suits people who want a few quiet days in the hills as well as darshan.

From the Indian side, every option starts at Kakarbhitta, about an hour from Siliguri, or at Bhadrapur airport, 50 minutes by air from Kathmandu. Ilam, 3–3.5 hours north on the Mechi Highway, makes the natural first night.

sections.heading: The climb from Kafle Pati, hour by hour
paras: The day starts early. Jeeps leave Phungling at about 2.30 a.m. and take 1.5–2.5 hours to reach Kafle Pati, where the motor road ends near a cluster of tea shops and lodges at about 2,750 m. From here a stone path and staircase climb roughly 1,000 m in about 5 km through fir, oak and rhododendron forest, with shelters and tea stalls along the way.

Most pilgrims take 4–5 hours up, stopping every 20–30 minutes, and reach the shrine between sunrise and mid-morning. The final section above the tree line is open, windy and cold, often below freezing before dawn even in October. After darshan, allow 2–3 hours to walk down, then drive back to Phungling for a late lunch. Ponies can be hired at Kafle Pati for part of the way up, at rates set locally that have been around ₹3,000–5,000 one way.

A cable car from Kafle Pati has been under construction for some years but has faced court cases and local protests, and it was not running when we last checked. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Helicopter shuttles and who should not fly
paras: In the pilgrim seasons, helicopter operators run shared shuttles to a landing area near the summit. From Phungling the flight takes only a few minutes, and local seat rates have been about NPR 10,000 return. From Kanyam, two hours from the border, it takes about 30 minutes each way, and seats have been quoted at about NPR 32,000–35,000 per person. Shuttles also fly from Phidim and Dharan.

Helicopters fly from first light until cloud builds, usually by late morning, and stop altogether in rain or high wind. At this altitude they carry fewer passengers, so families may fly in two groups and bags are limited to a small daypack. Time at the top is usually 30–45 minutes.

Because you land at almost 3,800 m without acclimatising, the following people should not fly: anyone with heart disease, lung disease or uncontrolled blood pressure, pregnant women, and infants. Healthy seniors usually manage well if they walk slowly to the shrine and come down promptly.

sections.heading: Best months and festival crowds
paras: October and November give the clearest views and the most stable weather, and March to May is the second season, with rhododendrons on the trail in March and April. December to February is cold and clear, but snow and ice can cover the upper steps for days after a storm, and helicopter shuttles run less often.

Navaratri and Dashain, usually in late September or October, bring the largest crowds of the year, with queues at the shrine that can last several hours and full hotels in Phungling. Saturdays and Nepali public holidays are also busy. June to September is the monsoon: landslides often close the Mechi Highway north of Ilam, the path is wet and leeches appear in the forest, so we do not run the yatra then.

sections.heading: What the yatra costs
paras: Our 6-day road yatra from Kakarbhitta or Bhadrapur starts from about ₹26,000 or US$300 per person for four pilgrims sharing a jeep and two twin rooms, with nights in Ilam and Phungling, a guide and a spare weather day. A couple travelling alone pays more, around ₹38,000 each, because the jeep is not shared. The 3-day helicopter yatra from Kanyam starts from about ₹38,000 per person, twin sharing, including a shared heli seat.

Budget separately for ponies, helicopter seats if you add them to the road trip, puja items, donations and tea on the path. Puja baskets with bells, cloth and incense are sold at Kafle Pati and Phungling, and prices rise near the temple. Carry small Nepali rupee notes. Indian ₹200 and ₹500 notes have been allowed in Nepal since late 2025 within a ₹25,000 limit, but check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: What to carry and how to prepare
paras: The climb is moderate to hard for most people, mainly because of the altitude. Walk slowly, drink water and do not rush the last section. Headache, nausea or unusual breathlessness are signs to stop and descend. People with known health conditions should speak to their doctor before booking.

At the shrine, remove shoes and leather items before entering the inner area, follow the queue and let the priests guide your offering. Photography of the deity is often discouraged, so ask first. Carry your rubbish back down: the path has few bins, and plastic left at the top is hard to clear.
list: Warm jacket, woollen cap and gloves for the pre-dawn start and the windy summit
Head torch with spare batteries, because the first 2 hours are walked in the dark
Light rain jacket, even in the dry season
Walking shoes with good grip for wet stone steps; a pair of walking poles helps on the way down
Two litres of water, dry fruit and biscuits
Personal medicines and a copy of prescriptions
Passport or voter ID for Indian citizens, and a birth certificate or school ID for children
Small notes in Nepali rupees for puja items, tea, pony fares and donations

faqs.q: How many days are needed for the Pathibhara yatra?
faqs.a: Plan 5–6 nights from the Kakarbhitta border by road: one night in Ilam, two or three in Phungling including a spare weather day, and one back in Ilam. With a helicopter shuttle from Kanyam, two nights from the border is enough. From Kathmandu, add a day at each end for the Bhadrapur flights.

faqs.q: How difficult is the climb to Pathibhara Devi?
faqs.a: Moderate to hard. The stone path from Kafle Pati gains about 1,000 m in roughly 5 km and ends at 3,794 m, where the air is thin. Most pilgrims take 4–5 hours up and 2–3 hours down. Walking slowly with rests every 20–30 minutes makes it manageable for anyone of reasonable fitness.

faqs.q: How much does the Pathibhara helicopter cost?
faqs.a: Shared shuttle seats have been quoted locally at about NPR 10,000 return from Phungling and about NPR 32,000–35,000 from Kanyam or Dharan. Our 3-day heli yatra from Kanyam starts from about ₹38,000 per person, including two hotel nights, car, guide and the seat. Fares change with fuel prices and season.

The shrine is open all year, but conditions decide what is practical. From June to September landslides often block the road from Ilam to Phungling. From December to February snow and ice can cover the upper path. October–November and March–May are the reliable seasons for both the climb and helicopter shuttles.

faqs.q: Can senior citizens visit Pathibhara Devi?
faqs.a: Yes. Many seniors visit every year, most often by helicopter shuttle or with a pony for the climb. The main risk is altitude at 3,794 m, so anyone with heart or lung disease or uncontrolled blood pressure should take medical advice first and should not fly straight to the top.

faqs.q: What is the route from Siliguri to Pathibhara?
faqs.a: Drive about an hour from Siliguri to the Panitanki–Kakarbhitta border, then 3–3.5 hours to Ilam for the first night. Next day drive about 160 km and 7–8 hours via Phidim to Phungling. From Phungling a jeep reaches Kafle Pati in 1.5–2.5 hours, and the walk to the shrine takes 4–5 hours.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a permit for Pathibhara?
faqs.a: No permit is needed to visit the temple. Indian citizens need a passport or voter ID to enter Nepal at Kakarbhitta, and children need a birth certificate or school ID. The Kanchenjunga restricted area permit applies only to trekkers going north of Phungling towards Ghunsa and the base camps. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where do pilgrims stay for Pathibhara?
faqs.a: Most stay in Phungling, where simple hotels offer clean rooms, hot water and vegetarian meals, and drive to Kafle Pati before dawn. Basic lodges at Kafle Pati save the early drive but are cold and very simple. On helicopter trips, families usually stay near Kanyam or Fikkal in the tea gardens.

faqs.q: Is there a cable car to Pathibhara?
faqs.a: A cable car from Kafle Pati towards the shrine has been under construction but has been held up by court cases and local protests, and it was not operating when we last checked. Until it opens, the choices are the walk, a pony for part of the climb or a helicopter shuttle. Check current status before you travel.
